articleTitle: An Efficient, Precise and User Friendly AI based Virtual Assistant
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) developments in recent years have enabled the creation of virtual assistants that can mimic human communication and interaction. The creation of a virtual assistant has the power to completely alter how people use technology. Using open-source technologies, a prototype virtual assistant system has been designed and implemented in this study. The virtual assistant will be able to interpret user requests using natural language processing (NLP) and speech recognition. Machine Learning (ML) algorithms have been used to increase the responsiveness and efficacy of the virtual assistant over time. To make it easier for users, the system also has a Graphical User Interface (GUI). Users won’t have to rely on conventional input devices like a keyboard or a mouse, allowing for more intuitive and natural interactions with technology. The virtual assistant may be used in a variety of fields, such as personal assistance, healthcare, education, and customer service. Based on the system’s precision, responsiveness, and user-experience, its performance has been assessed.

articleTitle: Checking the Truthfulness of News Channels using NLP Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Data analytics are difficult with unstructured data since it lacks pre-formatting, which makes up a large amount of information on social media. Research has looked into the potential of machine learning and natural language processing to interpret unstructured data and uncover significant information that could have gone unnoticed. We classify social media users using segmentation approaches on the basis of population, relationship status, and other criteria, allowing for the recognition of prominent people within particular categories. Behavior analysis assigns distinct roles to social media participants, such as users, recommenders, prospective users, and detractors, facilitating the tailoring of messages and reactions to address their concerns effectively. The study involves the accumulation of data from three news channels, data cleaning, and exploratory data analysis (EDA) to unearth patterns. Sentiment analysis is performed, and its results are compared for each of the news channels. Topic modeling is used to reveal different themes in the data. This study offers a solid basis for sentiment analysis and visualization, providing insightful information on the sentiment levels across various source kinds and features. It holds the potential to empower government agencies and businesses in harnessing the power of social media analytics for informed decision-making and improved communication strategies.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Piezoelectric PVDF Sensor With Copper, Graphene, Cobalt With PMMA for Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Energy harvesting is a major concern in today’s world because the existing electrical infrastructure is extremely wasteful in its use of energy. Today’s technologies used in electricity generation are not energy efficient. Piezoelectric sensors can convert physical energy into electrical energy efficiently and the process is cost efficient as well.Piezoelectric PVDF sensors with copper, graphene and cobalt along with addition of PMMA has been fabricated and the characterized for XRD, FTIR and SEM.. In XRD, beta phase is obtained to determine piezoelectricity. SEM images reveals porosity and thread like structure for better piezoelectricity. FTIR Peaks are obtained at 1399 & 1411 confirming PVDF. The results have been inferenced with a improvement in the properties of the PVDF material. The fabricated sensors are tested using an oscilloscope. The change is voltage is detected on application of pressure or vibrations on the sensor. PVDF demonstrates the highest piezoelectricity. It is used for energy harvesting which means that physical energy is utilized to produce an electrical energy to power electrical devices and equipments. Using IC LTC3588, on giving vibrations/pressure as the input to the PVDF sensor the generated voltage is rectified and amplified by the IC to light up the LED on the trainer kit, which requires a minimum of 3 Volts.In this paper, design, fabricate and characterize piezoelectric films is done and detected voltage from the fabricated films and perform energy harvesting by conversion of vibrational energy given to the film to electrical energy. Finally, results were compared by the addition of PMMA and without it

articleTitle: Efficient Battery Management For Solar Rechargeable Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Solar Rechargeable Autonomous vehicles are gaining remarkable recognition because to their Low Maintenance, Electrical Independence and Maximum Battery Life. A Solar Autonomous electric vehicle (SAEV) is a challenging task due to various complex learning processes that requires lot of coordination between mechanical components and electronic components. Mileage of SAEV is another significant task which has to be explored. To address the challenge and improve the performance of SAEV this paper proposes modeling of popular electric vehicles in MATLAB/Simulink. Simulations of a hybrid solar EV and conceptual solar EV model with heterogeneous battery packs are carried out using the Simulink model. The simulation results favor the implementation of concurrent battery packs at a reasonable cost. Furthermore, the selection of significant feasible solutions has also been focused on achieving the optimal performance for the proposed model. This paper proposes of using Vogel’s Approximation Method (VAM) for optimal battery management system. Different configurations are verified through standard evaluation measures like State of charge, Current, and voltage plots. The battery configuration also validated on MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Literature Review on Network Security Approaches using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: The Internet of Things facilitates the integration of communication systems and applications such as infrastructure management and environmental monitoring, so privacy and security techniques are crucial for the imminent of the Internet of Things. It empowers electronic devices around us to share information with other network members, recognize actions and vicissitudes in their environments, and perform independently without human interface. The swift development of the communication in Internet leads to larger networks and emerging security threats. In maintaining the confidentiality, integrity, and accessibility of data, intrusion detection systems (IDS) play a vital role by actively preventing network intrusions. Machine learning based IDS systems are becoming effective solutions for detecting network attacks.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Operational Transconductance Amplifier for Biomedical Applications using Cadence
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: The Operational Transconductance Amplifier (OTA) is a versatile and widely used electronic circuit that finds applications in various fields, including biomedical. This report provides a comprehensive review of OTA utilization in biomedical applications, highlighting its role in healthcare systems, medical devices, and bio-signal processing. The key characteristics and advantages of OTAs in the context of biomedical applications, including their high gain, high input impedance, and wide bandwidth. These characteristics make OTAs suitable for amplifying small biomedical signals with high precision, enabling improved signal quality and increased sensitivity in biomedical systems. The challenges and considerations in designing OTAs for biomedical applications, including power consumption, noise, and stability. These challenges need to be carefully addressed to ensure reliable and accurate signal amplification in biomedical systems. The importance of system-level design considerations when using OTAs in biomedical applications, including the choice of OTA specifications, integration with other system components, and overall system performance optimization

articleTitle: Plastic Detection and Picking Robotic Arm Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: the management of plastic trash is a global concern since it is difficult & expensive to manually sort waste. Scientists are developing and testing automatic sorting methods that enhance the effectiveness of the recycling process. In this paper, we present an effective and efficient robotic arm that detects plastic using a camera and classifies the object as recyclable plastic and non-recyclable plastic and effectively picks recyclable plastic. These automated sorting techniques make extensive use of machine learning algorithms which are trained using existing dataset. A pretrained ML algorithm was implemented with training accuracy of 89.6% and detection accuracy of nearly 60%, tested using real time images, live detection using a camera. Finally, we had integrated our customized pick and place robotic arm with ML algorithm

articleTitle: Live Wall: An AI based Visual Seeker Through Human tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Museums are educational and cultural institutions that intends to create narratives concerning nature, life, human, history, science, technology or any other field of human understanding. In creating these narratives, technology is always a great aid. Traditionally, timeline and linear narratives are like the staple storytelling tools in a museum. The point however is the resolution of change – how sensitive the system is, so that even a small shift of the control in linear dimension or the temporal scale can trigger a desired change in display. By developing several such linear scanning and correlated context-switching technologies, the National Council of Science Museums standardized the interactive reading wall technologies one of whose earlier versions have been reported in [10]. However, in those IR/ proximity sensor-based systems resolution always had a limit decided by the technology and the visitor had to move the control manually. In this paper we report two very significant HCI improvements that practically can revolutionize this essential museological tool – using the body as the controller or handler of the story and adoption of AI to achieve an accurate means to implement visitor-tracking.

articleTitle: Knowledge Sharing and Innovation Capability in a Telecommunications Company in the Kingdom of Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: This study investigated the relationship between individual, organizational, and information and communication technology (ICT) factors as enablers of knowledge-sharing processes and firm innovation capability (IC) for a telecommunications company in Bahrain. The study used simple random answers from 77 employees’ questionnaires and the partial least squares (PLS) structural equation modeling method. The results indicated that enjoyment of helping others significantly correlated with knowledge collection. Top management support was strongly associated with knowledge donation, which was also strongly linked to a company’s ability to innovate. Regarding the study’s implications, the company must change and add knowledge-sharing mechanisms to inspire innovation.

articleTitle: Adaptive Proximity Alert and Currency Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: This research presents a cutting-edge mobile application that leverages real-time GPS technology, the Google Maps API, and innovative geo-fencing techniques to tackle the common problem of passengers missing public transportation stops. Unlike traditional alarms, our app provides precise, personalized alerts, enhancing accessibility through features such as voice-enabled search and Optical Character Recognition (OCR). By addressing the challenges of inattention, this user-centric solution significantly improves the overall travel experience for commuters, especially those with diverse needs. Geo-fencing triggers alarms as users approach their stops, ensuring timely notifications. The OCR functionality aids visually impaired users, promoting inclusivity. Future enhancements, including advanced voice features, dynamic geo-fencing, and innovative voice-based ads, promise to further elevate travel experiences and accessibility within public transportation systems. Our research marks a significant step towards revolutionizing the way passengers engage with public transportation, enhancing convenience, and fostering a more inclusive transportation environment for all.

articleTitle: Analysis of triple ring resonator for detecting cholesterol level in the blood
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: A triple ring structure is designed on silicon on insulator with two straight waveguides and three ring waveguides. The designed structure operates in a mid-infrared region. The effective refractive index for the presence of cholesterol level is detected to be 1.55 at 1560nm in blood. The shift in the resonant peak of 120nm is observed as an analyte in the human blood. In the presence of light, detection is made easier with the coupling of triple ring structure, and it can also be monitored for quality factor and sensitivity. The sensor can be developed for implementing the design for a lab-on-a-chip device.

articleTitle: BrainCrossFed CNN Model for Alzheimer Classification using MRI data and Comparison and Benchmarking proposed model with DINOv2 and ExplainableAI using GradCAM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Alzheimer is one of the key mental illnesses suffered by 55 million people worldwide and 10 million new patients are added every year. If Alzheimer’s is detected in early stage, then the impact of disease will be reduced. Artificial intelligence (AI) models are helping in early diagnosis using MRI images. For better AI model development, the model needs to be trained over a huge dataset. But Health data privacy is another key concern of data collection, and hence federated learning framework helps models get trained over data without data transferring to cloud platform. Other Key concerns of AI model development is the availability of labeled data and benchmarking the model performance developed on dataset, which is trimmed or is a modified version. As availability of research work on specific data is rare. Currently, researchers have to develop other research models for specific data and such approaches take more time. Also, doctors expect explainability of the model, instead of black box model. Proposed BrainCrossFed model addresses data privacy concerns by avoiding the need for data transfer to cloud and leverage available labeled data at different federated nodes along with a dataset for Alzheimer to compute cross fed average of model weights. Due to the proposed Cross Fed Avg algorithm performance of the proposed deep learning model accuracy is increased from 99.11% to 99.77% close to 100%. Also such cross fed average enables the model to find global minima. Final performance achieved by the proposed model is 99.77%, with 100%. The performance of the model is benchmarked with current well known classification models, State-of-the-Art (SOTA), self supervised models like DINOv2 [1], for the same datasets. DINOv2 model has achieved 98%. Other generic well known models like ResNet101, DenseNet121, and Visual Geometry Group16 (VGG16) and customer models [2] have achieved max performance 97.60%. The GradCAM developed to explain the classification result.

articleTitle: Comparison of Machine Learning Models for Drought Prediction in Central Myanmar
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Drought is a highly dangerous natural hazard that causes water shortages, crop production losses, and environmental fires. Droughts are distinguished by meteorological metrics such as the standardized precipitation index (SPI). SPI is the most general and simple way to compute its values using only precipitation data. A popular way to determine the SPI is to fit the gamma function to rainfall data. The SPI of 14 sites was computed using monthly rainfall data over 33 years (1990--2022). The current study analyzed how well two well-known machine learning models, Random Forest (RF) and Decision Tree (DT), predicted the standardized precipitation index (SPI) across several time periods such as (1, 3, 6, 9, 12, 24) months. The models were built at the Nyaung Oo station in Myanmar’s drought-prone central region. Results proved that the proposed models could effectively predict droughts at the Nyaung Oo station. The Decision Tree model and Random Forest model recognized the SPI-12 values of Nyaung Oo station. In 80% of training and 20% of testing datasets, the RF model predicted the SPI better than the DT model, with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.19, a Mean Square Error (MSE) of 0.04, and the highest coefficient of determination ($R^{\mathbf{2}}$) of 0.97. The measurement accuracy is 0.96.

articleTitle: Glove Rupture Detection System using skin impedance.
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: At the time of surgery, the entire gloves will protect the surgeon from bloodborne antibodies and the surgical carving tools from bacteria on the skin of the physicians. However, glove prick is very common, and perforation rates are as high as 71%. When treating people with highly contagious diseases like AIDS, Hepatitis, there are extremely high chances of doctors being affected. This tool can be used for forensic investigations, laboratory testing, and other tasks in addition to performing surgical procedures. It can also be used by sewage cleaners. The goal of this project is to offer remedy to medical professionals who are exposed to numerous bacteria while performing procedures on patients using skin impedance to indicate puncture in the glove. The doctors are alerted to the puncture by finding it in a glove, enabling them to take the appropriate action.

articleTitle: An Innovative Simplistic Solar Powered Low-Cost Dry Waste Segregator Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative and straightforward approach to waste management through a solar-powered, low-cost robot designed for efficient dry waste segregation. The primary focus of this segregator robot design lies in its simplicity, affordability, and user-friendliness. By harnessing solar energy, it reduces reliance on conventional power sources and advocates for sustainable waste management practices. The system has successfully demonstrated the segregation of dry waste materials such as paper, metal, plastic, and glass, all automated for enhanced efficiency. The process begins with a blower positioned at the conveyor’s outset, effectively removing lightweight materials like paper. A rotatable electromagnetic system, equipped with two electromagnets, continuously moves over the conveyor belt, facilitating the separation of materials. To segregate plastic and glass, a density separator with a sieve is affixed to a container, with a servomotor for precise control. This setup efficiently removes floating plastic waste from the container, allowing for the subsequent collection of remaining glass waste. This technology exhibits substantial potential to revolutionize waste segregation procedures, boost recycling rates, and contribute to a more sustainable and environmentally conscious future.

articleTitle: IOT and Embedded Based Smart Baby Cradle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Internet of Things (IOT) and Embedded based smart cradle is a solution designed to enhance infant care and parental convenience. Embedding advanced instruments such as sensors, microcontrollers, and motors, it offers gentle and soothing motion to comfort babies, along with features like wetness detection and alert systems to promptly notify parents. This innovative cradle aims to create a safe and nurturing environment for babies while providing convenience and peace of mind to parents. The automated baby cradle described in this project utilized a microcontroller, a servo motor for gentle oscillations, a buzzer for parental alerts, a moisture sensor to detect wetness, and a sound-sensing system. The cradle is designed to provide convenience and safety for parents by automating the soothing motion of a baby’s cradle while incorporating a wetness detection system and a sound-sensing system. The controller Arduino Uno served as the central control unit, responsible for receiving input from the moisture sensor and controlling the mini servo motor’s oscillations. The mini servo motor is connected to the cradle, providing a gentle rocking motion to soothe the baby. The speed and intensity of the oscillations can be adjusted according to the baby’s preference. The automated baby cradle offers several benefits. Firstly, it provides a continuous and gentle rocking motion, simulating the feeling of being cradled in the arms of a caregiver, which can help soothe and comfort the baby. Secondly, the wetness detection system ensures, minimizing discomfort and reducing potential skin irritation to babies. We have additionally incorporated IOT-based smart system can also detect the emotions of babies by using a machine learning model (ML). Inference regarding baby cry can also be made via ML model. Lastly, the automation of the cradle’s motion and wetness detection and sound detection reduces the manual intervention required from the parents, allowing them to have more peace of mind and freedom to attend to other tasks

articleTitle: Smart Toll Collection: A GPS Based Automated System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: GPS-based toll collection systems have gained significant popularity in recent years due to their ability to provide seamless and efficient payment processing for highway and bridge tolls. These systems leverage the power of Global Positioning System (GPS) technology to precisely track and locate vehicles, enabling tolls to be collected electronically without the need for manual transactions. GPS-based toll collection systems have the benefit of high level of accuracy, which can be further tailored to accommodate various vehicle types and toll charges. Furthermore, these systems offer flexibility and scalability, easily adapting to fluctuating traffic volumes. In this innovative system, a GPS device is installed on the vehicle, establishing communication with a central server that calculates the toll fee based on the distance traveled. The fee is then deducted from a preloaded account linked to the vehicle owner or charged to a designated credit card. By eliminating the necessity for cash exchanges, this method not only enhances convenience for drivers but also reduces traffic congestion and saves valuable time and the environmental impact associated with traditional toll collection methods. Embracing this technology holds the potential to revolutionize the way tolls are managed and improve overall transportation experiences.

articleTitle: Correlation of Microhardness with Abrasive Wear of Thin Films: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Thin films find extensive applications in various industries, from electronics to aerospace, due to their unique properties and versatility. Understanding and predicting the mechanical behavior of these films, particularly their abrasive wear resistance, is crucial for optimizing their performance and longevity. This study explores the application of machine learning techniques to establish a correlation between microhardness, a fundamental mechanical property, and abrasive wear in thin films.Random Forest Regressor model was used to predict abrasive wear based on microhardness. The model’s performance was evaluated using Mean Squared Error and Root Mean Squared Error metrics.The results illustrated the feasibility of using machine learning to correlate microhardness with abrasive wear of thin films. Additionally, visualizations are presented that depict the predicted values against actual measurements, providing a clear representation of the model’s performance.

articleTitle: On the Reduction of Unnecessary Handovers Using 5G Small Cells in a 5G NR Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Nowadays, the deployment of 5G Non-StandAlone (NSA) networks has led to significant enhancements in the User Equipment (UE) experience, in particular in terms of latency reduction and throughput increase. To this end, 5G gNodeBs (gNBs) offer broad coverage but may face challenges in areas with low signal strength, resulting in a Quality of Service (QoS) degradation and too short connections to distant gNBs (denoted as Unnecessary HandOvers, UHOs) due to geographic peculiarities. In order to tackle these issues, in this paper the use of cost-effective 5G small cells in critical areas is considered, aiming at (i) boosting coverage, (ii) enhancing UE QoS, and (iii) avoiding UHOs, thus improving HO performance and UE QoS.

articleTitle: Reduced Area Search (RAS): An Algorithm to optimize path planning of Mobile Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: We present Reduced Area Search, an algorithm to optimize motion path planning. In the past few decades, optimal path planning has become prior for Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMR). Search-based algorithms like A* and Dijkstra are used for path planning on basis of search, similarly, sample-based algorithms like Rapidly-Exploring Random Tree (RRT), and Rapidly-Exploring Random Tree Star (RRT*) works based on sampling. The RAS algorithm reduces the area for search and sampling, reducing the exploration point, thereby minimizing time complexity.

articleTitle: Intelligent Safety Life Jacket Using Wsn Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: The body loses heat in hypothermia because it cannot maintain its internal temperature owing to a freezing environment. As a result, the body temperature will decrease rapidly. The person will lose consciousness or faint when the body temperature falls below 35°C. This study targets detecting climbers’ hypothermia and transmitting their health status to the climber’s group. It is difficult for mountain climbers to check their health and hypothermia symptoms for themselves and their climbing companions. To address this issue, we created a life jacket with an integrated hardware kit with a Peltier, temperature, and pulse sensor. LoRa Network is used to communicate with the climber’s group. Alert messages are delivered to mountaineers via the Android app and suitable protocols, which helps save the climbers if any discrepancies occur.

articleTitle: Experimental Thermal Performance Investigation of Evacuated Tube Solar Collector Using Nanoparticals under Cold Climatic Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: In this article experimental investigation of thermal performance of evacuated tube solar collector using nanoparticles under cold conditions investigated. The experimental performed under metrological condition of Bangalore, Karnataka, India. In experimentation three water based nanofluid namely aluminium oxide $(\mathrm{A}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3})$, Graphine oxide (GO) and strontium Carbonate $(\mathrm{S}_{r}\mathrm{A}\mathrm{D}-\mathrm{O})$ were used. The nanparticales with low concentration (mass basis) of 30, 60 and 90 mg were mixed with base fluid of water. A series of experiments were conducted to evaluate the thermal performance of evacuated tube. The average thermal efficiency of evacuated tube was found to be about 15.47%, 16.07% and 16.40% for 30 mg concentration of $\mathrm{A}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$, strontium Carbonate $(\mathrm{S}_{r}\mathrm{A}\mathrm{D}-\mathrm{O})$ and graphene oxide water based nanofluids, for 60 mg it was found to be 15.94%, 16.49% and 16.83%, similarly for 90 mg it was observed to be 16.32%, 17.40% and 17.57%, respectively. The results concludes that graphene oxide with 90 mg concentration gives better performance when compared with other combination of nanofluids. Further, it was observed that 90 mg graphene oxide based nanofluid gives about 12.36% improved thermal efficiency when evacuated working with water.

articleTitle: Efficient Model for Multiview classification for diagnosis of Brain Tumors.
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Brain tumors are caused mainly by DNA abnormalities, which result in aberrant cell division, prolonged cell lifespans, and the creation of aggregative masses inside the brain. Such tumors prevent the brain from operating at its best, sometimes resulting in long-term problems. These tumors’ genesis (primary or secondary) and malignancy (benign or malignant) are used to classify them. While some might not be immediately lethal, their growth or contact with healthy brain tissue might cause damage. Investigations into various approaches, such as conventional medical imaging and artificial intelligence (AI), mainly using deep learning (DL) and transfer learning (TL), is prompted by efforts to identify and categorize brain tumors. Implementing the EfficientNetB0 model, which is famous for its adaptability and efficacy, is an excellent demonstration of this strategy. This work uses a well-curated dataset of 3264 photos from various classes to closely analyze the use of the EfficientNetB0 TL model to identify and classify brain tumors from MRI scans. The model’s adaptability and accuracy are meticulously examined using a dual-pronged strategy incorporating transfer learning and fine-tuning, yielding an astounding accuracy of 98.5%. Accuracy and loss charts illustrate the model’s learning development in vivid detail, and a well-defined confusion matrix provides extensive insights into categorization effectiveness across various tumor classifications. The achievement of a 98.5% accuracy rate highlights the potential paradigm change made possible by AI and TL in the diagnosis and classification of brain tumors. This accomplishment confirms the efficacy of such sophisticated procedures and promises to speed up diagnosis, enable prompt therapies, and improve patient prognoses. The combination of AI and TL heralds a new era of precision medicine, ready to reshape the field of brain tumor care as research in this area grows.

articleTitle: Detection of Phishing Websites Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Internet and cloud technology improvements in recent years have significantly increased electronic trade, or consumer-to-consumer online transactions. The resources of an enterprise are harmed by this growth, which permits unauthorised access to sensitive information about users. One well-known assault that deceives users into accessing dangerous content and giving up their information is phishing. Most phishing websites use the same website interface and universal resource location (URL) as the legitimate websites. Phishing assaults are more likely to succeed on the Internet because of its anonymous and unregulated nature. Existing research demonstrates that the phishing detection system’s performance is constrained. An intelligent method is required to safeguard users against cyber-attacks. In this paper, we investigate the use of machine learning classifiers and a wrapper feature selection technique to detect phishing websites. The purpose of this study is to identify phishing URLs and to select the best performing machine learning algorithm by evaluating the accuracy rate, false positive and false negative rates of each algorithm.

articleTitle: Automobile Valuation Prediction Using Machine Learning based Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: With remarkable technological advancements and the emergence of new technical expertise, combined with substantial economic growth within our nation, there has been a noticeable shift in consumer preferences towards the purchase of automobiles, particularly cars, over other modes of transportation. This research paper aims to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the prevailing trends in used car pricing. Additionally, it endeavors to predict the prices of used cars using supervised machine learning algorithms. Considerable number of distinct attributes are examined for the reliable and accurate prediction. Also, it seeks to identify the most effective machine learning algorithm among those selected for the purpose of predicting car prices. Previous studies have already explored machine learning algorithms such as linear regression, multiple regression, and random forest in this context. Our objective is to assess which algorithm offers the most reliable and accurate predictions for car prices. This research has practical implications, as it can benefit first-time used car buyers by providing them with valuable insights into pricing dynamics. Furthermore, the model was evaluated using test data and the accuracy of 91% was obtained.

articleTitle: 3D Learning Experience Using Augmented Reality
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Technology-driven learning can significantly enhance the learning effectiveness for students of all ages, including those with learning disabilities. The extensive utilization of multimedia elements, such as graphics, audio, and video, has demonstrated considerable improvements and increased enthusiasm among learners. Augmented Reality serves as a link between theoretical and practical knowledge, enabling users to experience a blend of computer-generated virtual environments and real-world scenarios.This project aims to create a mobile application featuring different subsections, such as the solar system, human anatomy, and the skeletal framework. Utilizing AR technology, students can visualize these sections as 3D models. The application provides an immersive learning experience by allowing students to view objects as if they were real. Moreover, audio cues accompany the models, enhancing the interest and enjoyment in learning. The development process involves using software like Unity and Vuforia, along with C# scripting in Unity to bring the objects to life. The application employs the mobile phone’s camera to scan material and generate 3D models of the desired section for learning.The primary target audience for this application is students, with a particular focus on those with learning disabilities. The development process drew upon multiple references and research papers, which demonstrate its positive impact on students’ learning curve.

articleTitle: Classification of Various Cloud Attacks using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: The area of cloud computing is one that is extremely important in the realm of information technology. It truly gives the customer the option to access its services via the internet from a single platform. Virtual machines are necessary for CC. Every time a client makes a request, the server responds right away. Now a day’s cloud is adapted almost all over the globe, as it is a misconception that cloud platform is safe but due to public exposure of all the services as it is more prone to attacks which will eventually cause your data. In order to detect these kinds of threats several techniques are suggested by research. This paper delivers a ML based model which will predict the type of attack on cloud using different ML algorithms for the detection of these kinds of threats. We have applied three ML approaches namely Random Forest, KNN and SVM on an adequate dataset to estimate the type of attack. Random Forest shows outstanding performance with the accuracy 93.6% and recall value is also high.

articleTitle: Personalised Location Based Recommendation System Using Apache Spark
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Recommender systems play a very crucial role in our lives by suggesting the items users might be interested in without much provision from them. In recent times, the spike in internet usage and advancement in the Global Positioning System (GPS) has opened new avenues to explore the already thriving area of Location-based Services and provide recommendations based on them. The location-based recommendation has been lauded for its invaluable solution to information overload on the internet. This type of recommendation system aims to dispense service recommendations and product recommendations based on the profile as well as preferences of the users. Recommendation systems can be built in many ways and here, the aim is to do it using the PySpark framework that employs data from several sources including GPS, user reviews, and location-based searches to prove the recommendations. PySpark is used for managing the large datasets. In this paper first, we executed the ML algorithm which is the k-means algorithm and after that, we used the spark for the execution of the dataset where we used two algorithms ALS and SVD ++, and achieved an RMSE of 1.5 and 1.3 respectively

articleTitle: Test System Designing for Damping Control Unit
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: The automotive sector, particularly four-wheelers, is important to transportation in the modern world. The suspension system is what provides a smooth ride in a car.It is very important to test the suspension system, especially the damping control unit. PTS (Product Test Specifications) generation is one of several stages in the testing procedure for the electronic control unit (ECU). The communication interface and power supply were then put through functional and compatibility testing at the bench level. Microsoft Visio is used to construct the wiring and load box, and the LauterBach Debugger is utilized to carry out the flashing loading and upload the memory mapping to the ECU. The Embedded Test Specification (ETS) was subsequently created using the PTS in TestExec SOftware. Henceforth, the implementation of the data protection step using cyber security concept. The Venturi tester is used for the testing of the ECU. The calibration test for damping valves, the hot test, the cold test, and the short current measurement have been completed.

articleTitle: DNA Computing-Enabled Big Data Anonymization Framework with a Comparative Study through Existing Anonymization Tools
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Data anonymization is the process of transforming data so it protects the privacy of the individuals in the data. This is important for protecting the privacy of research participants, patients, and other individuals whose data is collected and used. There exists a number of anonymization tools in market. Though, these tools are not sure to be scalable to large datasets or may not offer the level of security essential for some requests or may not provide a flexible space for storage and retrieval. This paper presents a new big data anonymization framework that uses genetic operators for encryption and DNA computing for storage. The proposed framework is designed to be scalable to large datasets and to offer a high intensity of security. The paper also presents a comparative study of the proposed framework with existing anonymization tools. The study shows that the proposed framework is more scalable and secure than existing anonymization tools. The paper accomplishes that the proposed framework is a promising new approach to big data anonymization. The framework has the potential to be used in a various application, such as research, healthcare, and finance.

articleTitle: A study on Employee Perception of Artificial Intelligence in the Recruitment process of an IT Organization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: A study is conducted on employees’ perception of artificial intelligence in an organization’s hiring process. The objective of the research is to find out how employees perceive the importance of artificial intelligence in the recruiting process of an IT organization. The research design is descriptive in nature. Simple random sampling is used in the study and the sample size is 101. The data is collected using the questionnaire and the analysis is done using Chi- square, ANOVA and correlation. AI has been proven to provide a better candidate experience, reduce time to hire, and save time. Most employees agreed that procurement could be made faster by using AI. According to the study, the use of AI can also achieve unbiased applicant screening. AI helps the recruiters and is very important for better documentation, recruiting at scale, time and cost savings, automated interviews, etc.

articleTitle: A Survey on IOT Health Care Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) network comprises many type of smart objects which are the building elements for the creation of physically intelligent, all-pervasive structures. The IoT revolution is restructuring modern health care with well-known technologies and cutting-edge network systems or architectures, applications and industrial developments in IoT-based healthcare. To reduce the security risk, an intelligent collaborative security model is used with various innovations such as big data, wearables, and ambient intelligence can be leveraged in a health care context by addressing various IoT and e-Health policies and regulations around the globe to guage how they can contribute to the sustainable development of societies and economy by providing some ideas for further research on IoT based health-care based on a set of guiding principles. An intelligent collaborative security model is used to reduce security risk with various innovations like big data, wearables, and ambient intelligence can be used in a health care context by addressing different IoT and e-Health policies and regulations around the world to determine how they can help economies and societies in terms of sustainable development by providing some opportunities for further research on IoT based health-care depending on a set of guiding principles. The use of low cost Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) platform have grabbed some attention from the community of researchers in the past few years. In this study, we classify all recently published works based on how users can access FPGA design and embedded controller based on Raspberry Pi, Advanced RISC Machines (ARM), and Arduino platforms resources from anywhere from safe healthcare application utilized in IoT. A concept shortens the applications of momentarily unused resource for executing various tasks automatically. Their findings are highlighted, as well as their significant contributions.

articleTitle: Impact of Additive noise on Information loss characteristics of datasets
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: The prominence of the “big data” notion has dramatically contributed to the growing interest in data mining in recent years. Many different disciplines employ data mining, including business intelligence, scientific discovery, healthcare sectors, and many others as an application-driven discipline. Extraction of knowledge from a large data set is the goal of data mining activities. Although data mining can produce important information for several purposes, people are increasingly growing worried about data mining’s potential hazards to data privacy. To address such issues, privacy-preserving data mining (PPDM) has grown in popularity. The main goal of PPDM is to create data-mining methods that may be used on databases without invading people’s privacy. In this paper, original data was modified by applying additive noise on datasets and its impact on information characteristics are studied. The extent of dispersion or spread in the attribute values caused by noise was also examined. The mean variation error resulted from additive noise shifting the actual value. The median was more robust to outliers and noise, with less impact in additive noise. The mode values were affected minimally, causing data distribution shifts. The value of standard deviation increased.

articleTitle: YOLO V5 Deep Learning Model for Dental Problem Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Dental problems are a broad category of conditions that affect the teeth, gums, and other structures in the mouth. YOLOv5 (You Only Look Once, version 5) is a state-of-the-art object detection model, which can detect objects in an image in a single pass. This makes YOLOv5 very fast and efficient, making it ideal for real-time applications. This paper proposes to use YOLOv5 deep learning model to detect dental problems from panoramic X-Rays or Color images uploaded by a normal user or by dentist. Normal users can use it for initial consultation or for getting a second opinion. Dentists can use it for explaining the problem visually to a patient or to confirm his findings. The results of the experiment with around 8000 images has proved the use of YOLO v5 model predicts the problem to 90% accuracy. The paper also proposes to use YIQ model instead of regular RGB model which is better for medical imaging applications.

articleTitle: Impact of Multiplicative noise on Information loss characteristics of datasets
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: The rise of the “big data” notion has sparked a surge in interest in data mining across various disciplines, including business intelligence, scientific discovery, and healthcare. The primary objective is to gather information from large data sets. However, concerns about privacy have caused the rise of privacy-preserving data mining (PPDM), which aims to create data-mining methods without invading privacy. In this paper, original data was modified by applying multiplicative noise on datasets and studying its impact on the information characteristics of the datasets. The extent of dispersion or spread in the attribute values caused by noise was also examined. The multiplicative noise moved in the direction of distorting the difference between the newly added noise column and the original column of values, according to the mean variation error throughout the seed value. The median is more resistant to outliers and noise than the mean is. Although multiplicative noise caused considerable distortion, the median was comparatively constant compared to the mean. Multiplicative noise has alternate frequencies for mode values because it is more dependent on the scaling factors. The standard deviation is increased by scaling the values. Due to this, multiplicative noise also has data loss, which may lead to certain measurements becoming saturated or small-scale changes vanishing.

articleTitle: Enhancing Intrusion Detection Systems for Secure E-Commerce Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Rapid advancements in information and communication technologies have permeated various sectors, leading to an exponential growth in Internet users. However, this surge in connectivity has also given rise to a corresponding increase in cyber-attacks. E-commerce applications, which have become integral to our daily lives, encompass online banking, marketing, trading, and numerous other online businesses. To safeguard these critical systems and networks, Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) play a pivotal role by thwarting unauthorized access and countering various cyber threats. Presently, the prevailing NIDS systems predominantly rely on the Backward Oracle Matching (BOM) algorithm. While effective in reducing false alarms, this algorithm has been associated with a high packet drop ratio. In light of these limitations, this paper examines the existing NIDS systems and the various pattern-matching techniques they employ, shedding light on their weaknesses and constraints. To overcome these shortcomings, the paper introduces an enhanced iteration of the BOM algorithm. This enhanced version leverages multiple pattern-matching methods, enhancing the overall performance of the NIDS system and subsequently fortifying network security. To validate the proposed solution, comprehensive simulations were conducted using established datasets such as Snort and NSL-KDD. The experimental results unequivocally demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed solution compared to existing approaches. Specifically, it achieved a remarkable 5.17% improvement in detection rate while concurrently reducing the false alarm rate by 0.22% compared to the existing solution. IN summary, this paper addresses critical issues inherent in current NIDS systems, providing a robust solution through an enhanced BOM algorithm that incorporates multiple pattern- Matching methods. The experimental findings underscore the effectiveness of this approach in bolstering network security, offering promising prospects for mitigating cyber threats in the realm of E-commerce applications and beyond.

articleTitle: Analyzing Public Sentiment Towards LLM: A Twitter-Based Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: In this mixed-method research of tweets from December 2022 to April 2023 mentioning LLM, to optimize the data collection and analytics methods to focus on critical aspects. The set of information includes tweet content, usernames, locations, and sentiment indicators (positive tweets or negative tweets). The exploration into the Large Language Model’s (LLM) early users places an emphasis on the location details thereby providing insights about user spread without resorting to follower counts or user descriptions. On top of that, the study incorporates the establishment of major topics with the help of topic modeling techniques and analysis of sentiments linked with these tweets. Sentiment labels (positive or negative) are included as a distinct column within the dataset. Subjective insights into early users’ viewpoints and understandings are assembled through manual sampling and thematic segregation of tweets. Eventually, this refined approach allows for a comprehensive assessment into LLM’s reception, proficiency, and hurdles during the stated time period all while staying true to ethical practices regarding data gathering

articleTitle: Maximum Demand Forecasting in the Delhi Region using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: The National Capital Territory (NCT) of India, Delhi, is home to New Delhi, the country’s capital. Being a significant political and economic hub, Delhi experiences unique considerations in terms of power consumption. As of May 31st, 2023, the highest recorded power demand in Delhi occurred on June 29th, 2022, reaching a peak of 7770 MW. The dataset used in this paper is the daily Power-Supply-Position (PSP) reports generated by the NLDC, GRID Energy Sector, India which is a division of the Ministry of Power. This paper forecasts the maximum demand produced by Delhi taking in consideration of the Producers side by using various Machine Learning Algorithms with different pre-processing techniques such as data Imputation and Transformation Techniques and MAPE (mean-absolute-percentage-error) is used as a metric to evaluate models. The results suggest that Gradient Boosting Regressor with 7 days shift feature extraction gives the highest accuracy through Linear-Interpolation-imputation for univariate data.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Analysis of Lip-Reading Using Deep Learning Techniques: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Communication is a crucial aspect that occurs between a couple of people. Speech, consisting of audio-visual information, allows us to understand each other. Although individuals mainly rely on audio information to comprehend speech, visual details can enhance speech recognition, especially in noisy environments. Lip-reading is a phenomenon that can aid speech recognition systems by identifying the text spoken by an individual. To facilitate lip-reading, Automatic Lip-Reading (ALR) systems have been produced, using Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques such as Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL). This paper discusses the background behind lip-reading and delves into the workings of ALR systems, including the various DL and ML algorithms and popular English datasets used. The article presents a brief review of experiments conducted by other authors. Finally, the article is concluded by providing insights into the future scope of work.

articleTitle: Review on Internet addiction amongst college students by using Data Science and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Our reliance on technology has grown in numerous spheres of our lives as a result of easy access to communication and information technologies. But this incredible increase in Internet use has obviously been matched by an increase in problematic Internet use. Despite contentious arguments over its addictiveness, there is growing agreement that this hazardous behavior exists. We have examined seven of these studies that are directly related to internet addiction in this report. Internet usage offers numerous advantages, but it also has many concerns for people of all ages. Children and teenagers frequently utilise the Internet in their daily lives; hence, professional interventions should be used with this age group tailored to their particular developmental needs. Online risk exposure can have severe and enduring negative impacts.Based on literature review we can notice the most common questionnaire used for such study is the Internet Addiction Test (IAT), as well as the widely employed machine learning model for the same as observed in few papers is the Random Forest Algorithm for classification and regression. Few authors, investigated Several state-of-the-art models to determine the best results. Support Vector Machines served as the main classifier since they were the most accurate among the several classification techniques looked at. In this work a model is proposed that predicts if the level of addiction is low, moderate for high depending on the outcome of the questionnaire. The outcomes of the questions are trained using few ML Algorithms and the accuracy is measured.

articleTitle: IoT based Fruits and Vegetables Quality Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: To minimize food wastage, its cleanliness and safety may be a big concern. The food’s nutritional value should be discussed and upheld. This can be done using simple measures like Temperature, humidity, and terrain darkness. Therefore, implementing high-quality surveillance bias in retail stores is beneficial. These excellent monitoring systems monitor environmental problems that lead to food deterioration. The same climatic circumstances as refrigeration and storage for vacuums will be controlled. With this design, an identical food quality tester will be built, which can cover the fundamentals of the surroundings comparable to temperature, humidity, methane concentration, and light exposure.The device’s construction makes use of a microcontroller ESP 32 board as a medium to analyze the signals from the methane gas sensor and send an email alert to the user. The temperature and humidity sensor, which measures temperature and moisture content, and the methane gas sensor which monitors methane concentration, are both attached to the microcontroller. This will prevent the consumption of spoiled food and will help segregate it from consumable food.

articleTitle: Advancing Spelling Correction through Natural Language Processing and TextBlob: A Context-Aware Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: This study explores the development of an advanced spelling correction system using Natural Language Processing (NLP) and the TextBlob library. It addresses the prevalent issue of spelling errors in written text and aims to create a system that not only corrects typographical errors but also considers the contextual nuances in which words are used. The paper begins by explaining key NLP concepts, including tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and contextual analysis, which form the foundation of the spelling correction process. These techniques are crucial for systematically identifying and rectifying spelling errors. Furthermore, the research focuses on integrating TextBlob’s dictionary-based correction mechanism with contextual awareness to improve precision, particularly in context-dependent correction scenarios. The study rigorously evaluates the system’s performance through real-world testing and transparently discusses potential limitations and challenges encountered during development. Overall, the research paper highlights the transformative impact of NLP and TextBlob on spelling correction, demonstrating substantial improvements in correction accuracy and contextual comprehension. It emphasizes the wide-ranging applications of this technology, extending its influence beyond spelling correction to various domains, including word processing software, search engines, and virtual assistants. The findings endorse the effectiveness of this approach and call for continued research and development efforts to advance language processing technologies and enhance written communication across diverse applications.

articleTitle: MuteSign: Deep Learning-driven Sign Language Recognition for Inclusive communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Recognition of Sign Language is a typical area of experimentation, but it offers people with physical disabilities a great deal of convenience and support. Data collection, pre-processing, segmentation, feature extraction, and classification are just a few of the numerous steps that go into identifying sign language. Recurrent neural networks (RNN) with long short-term memory (LSTM) and convolutional neural networks (CNN) are two well-liked methods for recognizing sign language. CNNs are incredibly precise in their picture recognition and classification, while RNNs process sequential data extremely quickly. The significance of each frame is extracted by The Signs, which are programmed in two subunits called frames. The method involves dividing continuous signs into smaller components, referred to as frames, and deriving meaning from each frame.

articleTitle: Detection and Tracking of Multiple Faces in Video using Modified KLT Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: In proposed research, A system for accurate face detection and continual monitoring that makes use of face key characteristics as essential elements of the face that are incorporated in modified KLT approach. A greater degree of data is provided by video frames than by a single image. Critical attribute extractors (points) are used to automate the detection and monitoring of faces in a wide range of applications, such as human behavior identification, automated surveillance and human computer interface. By dividing the monitoring approach into three sections, one can construct a straightforward facial detection and continual monitoring system. Face detection, facial feature identification and tracking of faces are the first three steps. The Viola Jones object detector is used to achieve the face detection and modified KLT method is used to accomplish the continual monitoring. According to the findings of the investigation, our method is more reliable and effective at evaluating video frames to account for different types of occlusions and pose variations. Visual Tracker Benchmark database is used as a standard database. Further results are compared with staff database which was created to verify the outcomes. Average accuracy of 95% is obtained for the proposed method.

articleTitle: Automated Diagnosis of brain tumor classification and segmentation of MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Brain tumors are one of the most prevalent disorders of the central nervous system and are dangerous. For patients to receive the best treatment, early diagnosis is crucial. For radiologists to correctly detect brain tumor images, an automated approach is required. The identification procedure can be time-consuming and prone to mistakes. In this work, the issue of fully automated brain tumor classification and segmentation of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) including meningioma, glioma, pituitary and no tumor are taken into consideration. In this study, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (R-CNN) are proposed for classification and segmentation problems respectively. This study employed 3,200 images as training set and the system achieved an accuracy of 96% for classifying the tumors and 94% accuracy in segmentation of tumors.

articleTitle: Prediction of Student Perception Towards Current Educational Design Using Feature Selection and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Student perception is a vital part of the educational process since it has a direct influence on motivation, engagement, and overall academic achievement. Prior to COVID-19, the majority of education had a traditional approach, therefore there were few factors that may affect the perception of students. However, there was a significant influence on educational perception during the outbreak of COVID-19, since education was entirely transformed into online learning and eventually into a hybrid form. Therefore, it is crucial for educational institutions to comprehend these characteristics in order to give pupils a nurturing and enriching atmosphere. The objective of the article is to identify the factor that has the highest influence on students’ perception of the current educational system. Feature analysis is used in identifying the parameter that plays a great role in perception levels. Based on the information gathered through questionnaires, machine learning methods are used to forecast the degree of student perception. Thus, this research enables educational institutions to make data-driven choices that enhance the overall learning environment.

articleTitle: An Efficient and Resilient Technique for Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: The escalating complexity and rising volume of malware threats have necessitated the development of sophisticated and efficient techniques for analyzing malicious software. Machine learning algorithms have exhibited considerable promise in this realm, automating the process of malware analysis and un-covering previously unidentified malware samples. This research paper delves into the utilization of the random forest algorithm in malware analysis, utilizing a numerical dataset comprising a diverse set of malware attributes to train and assess the model. We employed a pre-processed dataset and implemented feature selection to enhance the model’s performance. Our findings demonstrate that the random forest algorithm achieved exceptional accuracy in the identification of malware samples. Furthermore, we conducted a comparison of the efficacy of the random forest algorithm with other widely used machine learning techniques in the field of malware analysis. The results suggest that the random forest algorithm proves to be a robust and effective method for detecting malware, with potential for further refinement through the incorporation of deep learning methodologies. This research holds significant implications for advancing automated tools for malware analysis and can substantially contribute to the ongoing efforts to combat malware threats.

articleTitle: Facial Emotion Recognition in Unconstrained Environments through Rank-Based Ensemble of Deep Learning Models using 1-Cycle Policy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: The field of Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) has advanced considerably in the last few years. Much research relies on lab-controlled datasets, characterized by limitations in size, quantity, and quality. These datasets feature high-resolution static images captured in ideal conditions but lack fidelity in representing real-world scenarios. Hence, FER systems must be trained on primary data that includes real-world scenarios like facial expressions captured from various angles and in different lighting conditions, images with occlusion etc., broadly termed as unconstrained environment. To leverage the gap, this study emphasizes utilizing an AffectNet dataset that has samples close to real-world scenarios. In addition, we propose a novel ensemble framework to increase the accuracy of emotion recognition by harnessing the complementary strengths of three distinct deep-learning models: DenseNet169, EfficientNetB7 and InceptionV3. The key innovation lies in our novel ranking-based fusion technique, which introduces a unique perspective on model confidence and its relationship with prediction quality. The rank-based fusion approach optimally harnesses each base model's unique characteristics and strengths. Our experiments confirm the ensemble framework's effectiveness, outperforming individual models in facial emotion recognition.

articleTitle: Liver Tumor Segmentation using Hybrid Residual Network and Conditional Random Fields
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Liver cancer is a leading cause to cancer-related death. The accurate delineation of the liver and its abnormalities is of utmost significance in the clinical interpretation and therapeutic strategizing of hepatic diseases. The primary objective of this study is to employ a hybrid residual network model, based on the U-Net architecture, for the automated segmentation of liver and liver cancers from abdominal Computed Tomography (CT) images. The U-shaped design and skip connections of the U-Net architecture make it particularly effective for CT image segmentation by combining high-level contextual information from the contracting path with fine-grained spatial features from the skip connections. Residual Networks (ResNets) utilize residual blocks to facilitate the construction of deep neural networks, therefore addressing the challenges posed by the vanishing gradient problem. The proposed methodology yielded dice global scores of 0.94 and 0.73 for liver segmentation and liver tumor segmentation, respectively on LiTS dataset. The findings demonstrate the exceptional performance and efficacy of the approach. The methodology also incorporates histogram equalization as a preprocessing strategy and utilizes conditional random fields as a postprocessing technique in order to improve the accuracy of segmentation.

articleTitle: Efficient Optimization Algorithm for IoT-based Cognitive Radio Routing Model with Energy Harvesting for Medical Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: In this research work, we focused to transmit medical data efficiently in the CR network with less consumption of energy, an effective routing scheme for the CR network has to be developed. The novel routing strategy is implemented by the Election-Based Optimization Algorithm (EBOA). This aids in the efficient transmission of medical data within the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) in a much faster and shortest way. Here, the cluster heads (CH) have to be selected in an optimal manner. The optimization of the CH is taken using the suggested EBOA. Initially, the selection of the CH takes place. The Energy Harvesting (EH)-based optimal shortest path determination by considering constraints such as “delay, energy cost, and distance” to enhance network lifetime. Evaluation of the implemented routing scheme for the CR network against classical algorithms is then followed to prove the efficacy of the executed routing strategy.

articleTitle: Design and Manufacturing of Cost-Effective Hand Exoskeleton for Paralysis Patient
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: The hand gestures required to pick up an object are predicted by sensors like Electromyography (EMG) in most of the hand exoskeletons. However, due to the sensor's noisy data, predicting hand gestures with it becomes challenging. Alternative hand gesture prediction technology, such as speech recognition, may be able to solve the aforementioned issue. An artificial intelligence technique called voice recognition translates speech input into written data. The objective of this research is to use voice recognition to create a low-cost hand exoskeleton for paralysed patients. The hand exoskeleton can provide shoulder, elbow, and finger movements for gripping an object. The user needs to speak the hand motion that he wants to employ to grab a certain object, and the hand exoskeleton takes it as a input. The microprocessor will direct the exoskeleton to perform the desired gesture once the gesture has been identified. The accuracy of anticipating a hand gesture using an EMG sensor and voice recognition are compared in the paper.

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient Cluster-Based Routing Protocol Techniques for Extending the Lifetime of Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Severe energy constraints are one of the most serious concerns in WSNs. Because the performance of Sensor Networks is greatly influenced by network lifespan, researchers are looking for a strategy to better utilize node energy supply while also extending network lifetime. The weather where the sensors are placed, the routing methods, etc., all affect how much battery is used. Numerous quality of service (QoS) metrics are provided to gauge the network’s performance and help reduce battery usage at the routing level. Many routing protocols have been proposed to address this issue. In this research, we analysed two low-power protocols—LEACH and Sub-cluster LEACH—and compared their performance. Levenberg-Marquardt neural networks (LMNNs) and Moth-Flame optimisation are both implemented one at a time to improve network performance. Energy efficiency, end-to-end latency, throughput, and packet delivery ratio (PDR) are some of the QoS indicators thought to assess performance. Sub-cluster LEACH with MFO was found to perform better than competing algorithms in post-implementation simulations. The simulation outcomes demonstrate that a suggested technique reduces energy consumption while extending life of WSNs.

articleTitle: Navigating College Campuses with Virtual Assistants
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Artificial intelligence plays a crucial role in everyday life. AI research is defined by computer science as the study of intelligent agents. Today, most individuals, whether on purpose or not, use some type of computerized information processing equipment. Artificial intelligence (AI) is already altering our way of life. A gadget that detects its environment and takes steps to increase the chance of reaching a goal. A database’s input can be a selection of users and articles, and the output is a harsh suggestion. The user can contribute input to the system either orally or textually. Voice assistants are software agents that can understand and respond to human speech using synthesized voices. The most popular voice assistants are Apple’s Siri, Amazon’s Alexa, Microsoft’s Crotona, and Google’s Assistant, which are incorporated in smart phones or specialized home speakers. Users may use voice commands to ask their assistants questions, operate home automation devices and media playback, and handle other basic chores like as email, to-do lists, and calendars. Artificial intelligence voice assistants can understand and respond to human speech. Users may use spoken commands to ask their assistant questions and perform other minor chores such as sending emails and browsing websites This study will look at the typical Usage of Voice Assistants in Educational Sector for Navigation Purpose.

articleTitle: Enhancing Contextual Understanding in GPT through Multimodal Pre-training
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Natural language processing (NLP) tasks that Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPT) have proven to be extremely effective at include text production, machine translation, and question answering. These models mostly rely on textual data, despite the fact that there is a lot of information available in other modalities such as images, audio, and video. In order to enhance the contextual comprehension of GPT models, this study will look into the benefits of multimodal pretraining. These massive models simply receive training on simple texts without any linguistic or global comprehension, regardless of their achievement. Furthermore, the bulk of large-scale models were trained using auto-regression. Because of this, this traditional way of fine-tuning performs terribly on future language comprehension exams.

articleTitle: A Review on Privacy Preserving Data Mining Techniques and Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on the Confluence of Advancements in Robotics, Vision and Interdisciplinary Technology Management (IC-RVITM)
abstract: Using techniques such as clustering, association rule mining, and classification, data mining can uncover hidden insights inside datasets.
